title: Cancel UPI AutoPay in PhonePe: Remove or Pause (2026)
metaDescription: Stop a UPI AutoPay mandate in PhonePe: open AutoPay under Payment Management, choose Pause or Remove AutoPay, then check that the status changed.
h1: How do you stop or pause UPI AutoPay in PhonePe?
summary: To stop a UPI AutoPay mandate in PhonePe, tap your profile picture on the home screen, open AutoPay under Payment Management, select the mandate and choose Remove AutoPay, or Pause if it is offered. PhonePe's help pages place the option under slightly different headings in some versions, so match the labels on your screen. Removing a mandate stops future debits but does not end your subscription with the merchant, so cancel there too.

steps.name: Tap your profile picture
steps.text: On the PhonePe home screen, tap your profile picture at the top of the screen.

steps.name: Open AutoPay
steps.text: Scroll to the Payment Management section and tap AutoPay. Some PhonePe help pages place it under Payments Settings or AutoPay Settings instead.

steps.name: Select the mandate
steps.text: Tap the AutoPay you want to stop, and check the merchant name, amount and next debit date before you continue.

steps.name: Choose Pause or Remove
steps.text: Pause is described in PhonePe's help page, so use it if you may want the service back. To end the mandate, choose Remove AutoPay. If Pause is not on your screen, removal is the only in-app choice.

steps.name: Confirm the change
steps.text: Finish the confirmation. It may ask for your UPI PIN, so have it ready.

steps.name: Check the status
steps.text: Reopen AutoPay after a few minutes. If the mandate still shows as active, contact PhonePe support with a screenshot.

stepsHeading: How to remove or pause AutoPay in PhonePe

sections.heading: Where PhonePe keeps AutoPay
paragraphs: PhonePe's help page on AutoPay authorised for external merchant platforms gives the route as profile picture, then AutoPay under Payment Management, then Pause or Remove AutoPay. A second PhonePe help page uses Payments Settings and AutoPay Settings, with a Delete option, so the wording on your screen is the guide.

PhonePe's help content also says you can delete the AutoPay from the merchant's own app or website. That helps when the merchant's screen shows the subscription more clearly. Check the mandate in PhonePe afterwards either way.

sections.heading: Pause or remove: which one to choose
paragraphs: Remove AutoPay ends the mandate. If you want the service back later, you will need to set up AutoPay again when you restart the subscription. Pause suits a short break or a seasonal service, provided it appears for your mandate.

Third-party guides disagree on whether every PhonePe version offers Pause. One says the app only lets you delete, which conflicts with PhonePe's own page. Decide before you tap, because removal may be the only option on your version.

sections.heading: The debit that is already scheduled
paragraphs: The PhonePe help pages checked for this guide do not say how a debit that is already scheduled is handled. Third-party guides say a debit queued a few days ahead may still go through, so check the next debit date in the mandate details first. If it is close, also ask the merchant to skip the next charge.
HDFC Bank's guide to UPI AutoPay says cancelling stops future debits and that payments already completed are not reversed. Ask the merchant about any refund for a debit that has gone through.

sections.heading: Problems that stop the change
paragraphs: The most common problem is AutoPay not appearing in the menu. Third-party guides say older versions may not show the mandate options, so update the app. A mandate approved in another UPI app will not appear in PhonePe, so check that app as well.

HDFC Bank says debt collection and loan repayment mandates cannot be cancelled through a UPI app, so contact the lender directly for those. If PhonePe will not update the status, use the Help section in the app or contact PhonePe support.

sections.heading: Subscriptions billed through other routes
paragraphs: Removing the mandate does not cancel the service. If the same service is billed through Google Play or the App Store, cancel it in that store's subscription settings. A card that the merchant keeps on file has to be stopped with the merchant or your card issuer.
Once you have cancelled everywhere, wait for the next billing date to pass without a charge. That is the clearest sign the stop has worked.

sections.heading: Where Essara fits in
paragraphs: PhonePe is one of several places where a mandate can sit, so a single list helps. In Essara you record each mandate yourself with its amount and frequency, and see the auto-debits due this week and month. Essara does not read PhonePe, your bank or your SMS, so the pause or removal still has to be done in the app.

faqs.q: Can I pause AutoPay in PhonePe?
faqs.a: PhonePe's help page describes a Pause option next to Remove AutoPay. A third-party guide says the app only offers deletion, so check the label on your own version before you tap. If only Remove appears, removal is the only in-app choice.

faqs.q: Does removing AutoPay in PhonePe get my money back?
faqs.a: No. Removing a mandate stops future debits but does not reverse a payment that has already gone through. Ask the merchant about a refund, and contact PhonePe support if you believe a debit was not authorised.

faqs.q: Why does my AutoPay still show after I removed it?
faqs.a: The status can take a few minutes to update. If it still shows as active, check whether a debit is already queued for the next date, then contact PhonePe support with the mandate details and a screenshot.

faqs.q: Can I stop PhonePe AutoPay from the merchant's side?
faqs.a: PhonePe's help page says you can log in to the merchant's app or website and delete the AutoPay there. Afterwards, reopen AutoPay in PhonePe to confirm the mandate is no longer active.

faqs.q: Is a PhonePe Wallet top-up the same as AutoPay?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. PhonePe's help results describe Wallet auto top-up as a separate setting under PhonePe Wallet, so look there first if the debit is a wallet top-up rather than a merchant mandate.
